title: Height-one valuation comparison for Noetherian ind-etale domains
statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative Noetherian normal domains [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], meaning a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras of finite presentation. Then $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and injective. For each prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$, put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. The local map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] satisfies
$$\dim A_{\mathfrak p}=\dim B_{\mathfrak q},\qquad \mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}.$$
Here dimension is the supremum of lengths of strict chains of prime ideals. In particular, if $\mathfrak q$ has height one, so does $\mathfrak p$; both local rings are discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], a uniformizer of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ maps to a uniformizer of $B_{\mathfrak q}$, and, for the induced embedding of fraction fields,
$$v_{\mathfrak q}(\varphi(f))=v_{\mathfrak p}(f)\qquad(f\in\operatorname{Frac}(A)^\times).$$
The valuations are normalized to assign value one to a uniformizer. No finiteness of $B$ as an $A$-module, excellence, or henselian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent-extracted local algebra consequence of Tag 0AH1 (lemma-filtered-colimit-etale-noetherian-fibres): its reduced zero-dimensional fibres, together with flatness and going down, give the dimension and maximal-ideal comparisons; the DVR assertion is their codimension-one consequence.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], $\varphi$ is weakly etale, hence flat by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. For $0\ne a\in A$, the sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{a}A$ is exact because $A$ is a domain. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] with the flat $A$-module $B$ shows that multiplication by $\varphi(a)$ on $B$ is injective. If $\varphi(a)=0$, this sends both $0$ and $1$ to zero, contradicting $0\ne1$ in the domain $B$. Thus $\ker\varphi=0$, and the induced fraction-field map is the embedding $a/b\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(b)$.

source.place: Tag 097N (lemma-ind-etale-implies); Algebra Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), tensor exactness; injectivity argument written out

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q\subset B$ and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S=B_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps], $R\to S$, $a/s\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(s)$, is flat and local and both rings are Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] both are normal domains, with fraction fields $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ respectively. The map is injective: its composite into $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ is the fraction-field embedding of Step 1 restricted to $R$.

Choose the filtered presentation of $B$ by finitely presented etale $A$-algebras supplied by the ind-etale hypothesis. Since $B$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-finite-separable-fibres] applies to this presentation and to $\mathfrak p$: the canonical map identifies $C=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $\prod_{j=1}^r\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$, where the $\mathfrak q_j$ are precisely the primes of $B$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. Our chosen $\mathfrak q$ is one of them, say $\mathfrak q_j$, so $r\ge1$. Write $Q$ for the kernel of projection $C\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, a prime of $C$.

We spell out the local fibre. Let $T=\varphi(A\setminus\mathfrak p)$ and $B_{\mathfrak p}=T^{-1}B$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $C=B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-residue-fields], $Q$ corresponds to $\mathfrak q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] to $B_{\mathfrak p}$, its ideal $\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$, and $Q$. Its inverse image is $\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak p}$: membership of $b/t$ is equivalent to $b\in\mathfrak q$, since $t\notin\mathfrak q$. Moreover $(B_{\mathfrak p})_{\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak p}}=S$: the fraction $(b/t)/(c/u)$ goes to $bu/(tc)$, and the inverse sends $b/c$ to $(b/1)/(c/1)$. The cited quotient isomorphism therefore gives $S/\mathfrak pS\cong C_Q$. In the product of Step 3, the idempotent $e_j$ with coordinate $1$ at $j$ and $0$ elsewhere lies outside $Q$; inverting it kills all other factors. The remaining factor is already a field, so $C_Q\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Thus $S/\mathfrak pS$ is a field. Since $S$ is local and $\mathfrak pS\subseteq\mathfrak qS$, its unique maximal ideal is $\mathfrak pS=\mathfrak qS$.

source.place: Tags 00E6 (remark-fundamental-diagram), 0H9M (remark-local-ring-fibre), 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), and 00OL (definition-fibre); explicit fraction and product calculations

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to the flat map of Noetherian rings $A\to B$ at $\mathfrak q$. It gives $\dim S=\dim R+\dim(S/\mathfrak pS)$. The quotient in Step 4 is a nonzero field, whose only prime is $(0)$, so its dimension is zero. Hence $\dim R=\dim S$. The same cited statement identifies these dimensions with the heights of $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$ respectively, proving all the dimension assertions, including that height one of $\mathfrak q$ implies height one of $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total), flat case; field dimension computed directly

proof.text: Now suppose $\mathfrak q$ has height one. Step 2 gives Noetherian normal local domains $R,S$, and Step 5 gives dimension one for both. Applying [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] to each proves that both are discrete valuation rings. If $\pi$ is a uniformizer of $R$, then $\mathfrak pR=\pi R$ by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Extending this ideal along $R\to S$ and using Step 4 gives $\mathfrak qS=\mathfrak pS=\varphi(\pi)S$, where $\varphi$ here denotes the localized map. Thus $\varphi(\pi)$ is a uniformizer of $S$.

For $f\in\operatorname{Frac}(A)^\times=\operatorname{Frac}(R)^\times$, write $f=a/b$ with $a,b\in R\setminus\{0\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], $a=u\pi^m$ and $b=w\pi^n$ with $u,w\in R^\times$ and $m,n\ge0$. A ring map sends units to units: $\varphi(u)\varphi(u^{-1})=1$, and likewise for $w$. For a normalized DVR valuation, units have value zero (both the unit and its inverse lie in the valuation ring and have nonnegative values), while a uniformizer has value one. Step 6 makes $\varphi(\pi)$ a uniformizer, so $v_{\mathfrak p}(f)=m-n$ and $v_{\mathfrak q}(\varphi(f))=v_{\mathfrak q}(\varphi(u)/\varphi(w))+(m-n)v_{\mathfrak q}(\varphi(\pi))=m-n$. This proves the asserted equality also for negative exponents. The only hypotheses used were those of the statement.
